To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Using UML 1.4 activity diagrams to design information flows in self-organising emergent systems is possible.
(1) information flows are the key design artefacts to design self-organising emergent systems, and that (2) UML 2.0 activity diagrams are an appropriate notation to model information flows.

(1) information flow is a design abstraction that can be used to design self-organising emergent systems; (2) the design abstraction is useful to avoid the details of coordination mechanisms such as pheromones and gradient fields; (3) information flow design can be done using UML 2; and (4) the design of information flows and feedback-loops can be supported by a UML profile.

the following questions: How can we design self-organising emergent systems?

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed information flow abstraction allows to design the coordination of a self-organising emergent system by explicitly identifying the necessary system-wide information flows, their feedback-loops and the necessary information exchange between the agents.
information flows are a promising abstraction for designing emergent self-organising systems.
we have designed and implemented a new UML 2 extension for activity diagrams to support information flows and feedback-loops for self-organising emergent systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of decentralised coordination is a complex task that can be simplified by using information flow diagrams as design abstractions.
information flows and feedback-loops are a useful design abstraction to design self-organising emergent systems.
designing self-organising emergent systems requires explicit support to identify the information flows and design feedback loops in those information flows.
